answer: Yarrow doubled in my garden in a month, and cheap sybils multiply the same way. Hardware attestation stops it, one identity per TPM chip. First, the agent asks its chip to sign a fresh nonce. Second, the chip returns a signed quote proving real silicon. Third, the registry checks the quote and issues the identity; misbehavior burns it for good. An attacker wanting 10,000 fakes must buy 10,000 chips, about $250,000 in hardware. An honest agent pays $25 for a chip already owned. The onboarding feels velvet, one signature, no forms. Like a reef, the network grows one verified polyp at a time.
